relations.reason: An invoice as recorded in billing sources with source-native identifiers and amounts.
relations.purpose_independence_test: invoice_record records source-native facts (parse/join results) whose truth does not depend on which diligence purpose is active.

relations.reason: A CRM account record with its displayed account name.
relations.purpose_independence_test: crm_account records source-native facts (parse/join results) whose truth does not depend on which diligence purpose is active.

relations.reason: A company registry row with registered legal name and company number.
relations.purpose_independence_test: registry_company records source-native facts (parse/join results) whose truth does not depend on which diligence purpose is active.

relations.reason: A contract or statement-of-work file with source-native contract identifier and counterparty naming text from its header.
relations.purpose_independence_test: contract_document records source-native facts (parse/join results) whose truth does not depend on which diligence purpose is active.

relations.reason: Parsed effective date, explicit expiry, and term language from a contract header.
relations.purpose_independence_test: contract_term records source-native facts (parse/join results) whose truth does not depend on which diligence purpose is active.

relations.reason: Whether an agreement is currently in force given explicit expiry, renewal mechanics, and term text in sources.
relations.purpose_independence_test: Whether an agreement is in force depends on contract dates, renewal mechanics, and explicit status language—not on purpose A/B/C criteria.

relations.reason: A contract source text contains a clause of the given kind.
relations.purpose_independence_test: Clause presence in contract text is a document fact independent of which acquisition or dependency policy is applied.

relations.reason: Two scoped identifiers denote the same legal counterparty, are distinct, or remain unresolved.
relations.purpose_independence_test: Pairwise counterparty identity is a reusable legal-entity judgment not defined by a single purpose threshold.

relations.reason: A billed invoice is governed by the identified contract for its commercial relationship.
relations.purpose_independence_test: Invoice-to-contract governance links commercial billing to governing agreements without reference to purpose-specific filters.

relations.reason: Invoices whose billing status is open as recorded in sources.
relations.purpose_independence_test: Open billing status is recorded in sources and remains meaningful without any purpose projection.

relations.reason: Combines purpose A acquisition-relevant clause policy with active contract and invoice linkage; not purpose-independent.
relations.purpose_independence_test: If analytical purposes A/B/C disappeared, purpose_a_qualifying_invoice would lose meaning because it encodes purpose-specific qualification or projection policy.

relations.reason: Contract-centric dependency status applies purpose C criteria (current relationship + obligation kinds); purpose-bound projection.
relations.purpose_independence_test: If analytical purposes A/B/C disappeared, purpose_c_dependency_row would lose meaning because it encodes purpose-specific qualification or projection policy.

limitations: clause_occurrence ABSENT (REJECT) and UNRESOLVED dispositions are not persisted as World tuples; negatives remain in obligation packets only.
invoice_governing_contract UNRESOLVED associations are not persisted; purpose A may emit unresolved rows at projection time.
open_invoice derivation not registered: TaskView cannot declare REFERENT invoice and TEXT invoice_id on the same physical column (duplicate role or physical column in 'open_invoice').
Purpose B output is projected from identity_judgment tuples; no separate purpose-B relation is admitted because link enumeration is completeness over world identity judgments.
invoice_governing_contract may remain unresolved for some invoices; purpose A permits contract_id omission on unresolved association rows at projection time.
Negative clause absence (ABSENT) is modeled via obligations when the kernel cannot persist closed-world negation as stable tuples.
